pr_title: *: support user defined variable and SET clause in LOAD DATA statement
pr_body:
According to [MySQL Manual](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/load-data.html) `LOAD DATA` statement support user defined variable and SET cluase.
And To keep up the pace with [pingcap/parser](https://github.com/pingcap/parser) which has already got a [PR](https://github.com/pingcap/parser/pull/288) to implement it long days ago.

<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #16617, #11941 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary: User defined variables and `SET` clause didn't work well in `LOAD DATA` statement.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed: 
Inside `executor/load_data.go` add a new struct `FieldMapping` consists table column or user defined variable.

How it Works:
>  By default, when no column list is provided at the end of the `LOAD DATA` statement, input lines are expected to contain a field for each table column. If you want to load only some of a table's columns, specify a column list.
[MySQL Manual](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/load-data.html)

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Integration test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- Support mixed specification of table column and user variable in `LOAD DATA` statement.
- `SET` clause support input field preprocessing in `LOAD DATA` statement.

issue_context.title: server: set clause in load data will not take effect and tidb does not report error
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. What did you do?

```
CREATE TABLE `i3` (
  `c1` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `c2` int(11) DEFAULT NULL
)

cat data 
1,100
2,100

mysql> LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '/data' INTO TABLE i3 FIELDS TERMINATED BY ',' ENCLOSED BY '' LINES TERMINATED BY '\n'(c1, @val) set c2=cast(@val as signed);
Query OK, 2 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Records: 2  Deleted: 0  Skipped: 0  Warnings: 0

mysql> select * from i3;                                                               
+------+------+
| c1   | c2   |
+------+------+
|    1 | NULL |
|    2 | NULL |
+------+------+
2 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

<!-- If possible, provide a recipe for reproducing the error. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see?

```
mysql> select * from i3;
+------+------+
| c1   | c2   |
+------+------+
|    1 |  100 |
|    2 |  100 |
+------+------+
2 rows in set (0.00 sec)

```

### 3. What did you see instead?

```
mysql> select * from i3;                                                               
+------+------+
| c1   | c2   |
+------+------+
|    1 | NULL |
|    2 | NULL |
+------+------+
2 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

### 4. What version of TiDB are you using? (`tidb-server -V` or run `select tidb_version();` on TiDB)
Release Version: v4.0.0-rc
